# Hook sequences

One file per scenario, read by `tests/unit/test_session_state_machine.py`. They are generated by
`scripts/gen_hook_fixtures.py` (run by hand; tests never write them).

Each file is `{"scenario", "origin", "pid", "events": [{"received_at_ns", "payload", "expect"}]}`. The test
turns every payload into an envelope the way `fylgja hook` builds it, normalizes it with the real
`fylgja.collectors.claude.normalize` and feeds it to the state engine. `expect` is the state the session of
that event must have afterwards.

| File | Origin | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| `probe-session.json` | `tests/fixtures/ratatosk/probe-session` | prompt, tool, `PostToolUse`, `PermissionRequest` plus its `Notification`, three turns, `SessionEnd` |
| `interrupt-session.json` | `tests/fixtures/ratatosk/interrupt-session` | a prompt that never reaches `Stop` |
| `stopfailure-session.json` | `tests/fixtures/ratatosk/stopfailure-session` | `StopFailure` gives `error` |
| `clear-model-session.json` | `tests/fixtures/ratatosk/clear-model-session` | `SessionEnd` with reason `clear`, then a new session id in the same process (A11) |
| `synthesized-hooks-docs.json` | synthesized | every Notification type of R9, `PermissionDenied`, `PostToolUseFailure`, an idle prompt after an unseen finished turn, events that name no state |

The ratatosk summaries hold event names, tool names, reasons and payload *keys*, not payloads, so the payload
values are placeholders (`/work/...`, `placeholder prompt`) and the session ids are synthetic. The synthesized
sequence follows the current hooks documentation. **Fresh live captures are a by-hand follow-up**: capture a
throwaway Claude session's hooks with `fylgja hook`, sanitize them with `scripts/sanitize_fixture.py`, and add a
scenario to the generator. Do not start a Claude session from a test or a pipeline step.
